story.title: China reportedly recruited AI exec to spy on Jensen Huang

facts.text: Last week, the NYT reported that Jensen Huang was seen as the target of a “Chinese spy plot” and shared details about Alice Huang and Jensen Huang’s relationship, but the information that China’s MSS had recruited her is new.

Further, it can't be confirmed where she is now or whether she still holds a top executive role at Megaspeed.Chinese Embassy in US rejects allegationsWSJ reported that the Chinese Embassy in Washington rejected the allegations, saying that Beijing opposes what it described as the peddling of a "Chinese spy narrative" and adding that the country's technological development is grounded in "independent innovation."An Nvidia spokesperson said, "We’re confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," and added that CEO Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice "are not unusual or unexpected” given their business ties.A representative of the Singapore Police Force said investigations into Megaspeed were ongoing and declined to give specifics.

Alice Huang, who also goes by Huang Le, isn't related to Jensen Huang.Who is Alice Huang?According to a 2025 New York Times report, Alice Huang has a scant online profile, but she has spent much of her career in China, which included working as a television reporter for Chinese state media.

Washington DC: The Chinese businesswoman, with whom Nvidia's Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jensen Huang had alleged ties, was recruited as a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, The New York Times reported, citing a memo circulated among policymakers in the Trump administration.On Friday, three House Republican committee chairs have asked Nvidia CEO to address, behind closed doors, the reported links with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of providing information to Beijing, Axios reported.Nvidia has denied the allegations as baseless .A top executive at a Singapore-based data centre firm named Megaspeed faced intense scrutiny over potential involvement in diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips towards China, as outlined in a report by The New York Times.
As per the report, the Nvidia chief executive successfully lobbied the administration during Trump's second term to reverse stricter export controls governing the company's chip shipments to China.
I've always found Jensen Huang to be very aboveboard.
The investigation also revealed that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a Chinese citizen, had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive.

The situation is further complicated by Jensen Huang's reported access to Trump's thinking on an issue of critical importance to both countries, particularly as the US president prepares to visit China next month.
Now, according to a report by The New York Times, American intelligence officials have concluded that she was possibly a Chinese intelligence asset, passing information to Beijing.

While some firms have allegedly smuggled chips across the Chinese border, others have legally established businesses in Southeast Asia that purchase large quantities of chips to build data centres serving Chinese companies.
The parent company of Inspur had been blacklisted by the US government over allegations of supplying technology to the Chinese military.

With Huang's encouragement, Trump has reportedly enacted industry-friendly chip and AI policies, along with approving some sales of previous Nvidia chips to Beijing while negotiating with his counterpart Xi Jinping.In late 2024, officials from the US Commerce Department started investigating whether the Singapore-based Megaspeed was involved in diverting Nvidia's chips to China, bypassing Washington's export controls meant to protect crucial technologies.US security experts have raised concerns that companies may be bypassing restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips by setting up data centres in neighbouring countries and offering Chinese businesses remote access to their computing power.
